concepts.summary: The basis and cobasis are defined arbitrage spreads between futures and spot prices that reveal market conditions of abundance or scarcity.

Cobasis = spot (bid) – future (offer)
It is not mathematically or physically possible for both basis and cobasis to be positive.

concepts.title: Basis-Cobasis Price Discovery Mechanism
concepts.summary: Futures buyers pushing up prices widen the basis, prompting warehousemen to buy metal, causing spot prices to follow with a lag.
evidence_quotes: The more the buyers in the futures market push up the price of gold contracts, the more the warehousemen pull up the price of gold metal – and the more this spread widens.
In other words, gold tends to be scarcer at lower prices and more abundant at higher prices.
This shows that the price rise was driven by speculators in the futures market, whose demand is pulled into the spot market by the arbitrage of carrying gold.

concepts.title: Monetary Metals Fundamental Price Model
concepts.summary: A model estimating what gold and silver prices would be absent speculative influence, based on basis/cobasis data.
evidence_quotes: What if one could use the basis to build a model to look at what the price of the metal would be, absent the speculators?
Monetary Metals has built this model.
We calculate a fundamental price – if silver metal were clearing without speculators influencing the price one way or the other – of USD 25.22.

concepts.title: Gold-Silver Relative Scarcity Ratio
concepts.summary: Comparing gold and silver cobasis-to-basis ratios indicates which metal is relatively scarcer in the market over time.
evidence_quotes: For the last year, the ratio of the gold cobasis…to silver cobasis has been above the ratio of the gold basis to silver basis.
This means gold has been the scarcer metal, to the market.
As of April 28, this reversed. The ratios are farther in silver’s favor than they’ve been in a year

concepts.title: Interest Rates and Gold Price Relationship
concepts.summary: The text argues no direct correlation exists between interest rates and gold prices, citing historical divergences and current risk dynamics.
evidence_quotes: There is not a direct correlation between the interest rate and the gold price.
We had rising rates in the 1970s, and rising gold prices. And we had falling rates post2001, and rising gold prices.
However, during this time the Federal Reserve hiked the interest rate. Libor went up from around 0.3% to around 1.3%!

concepts.title: Sovereign Credit Risk Driving Gold Demand
concepts.summary: Rising government debt levels without matching repayment capacity increase creditor risk, pushing investors toward gold as a default-avoidance asset.
evidence_quotes: we have had a major increase in the risk of being a creditor to governments. Their debt levels have skyrocketed, but not their capacity to pay those debts.
When you own gold, there is no counterparty and you have no worries about credit default.
The economic and interest rate situation is not likely to improve. Therefore, people will keep turning to gold.

concepts.title: Wealthy vs Poor Gold and Silver Demand
concepts.summary: Gold demand comes from wealthy investors selling other assets, while silver demand relies on wage earners' disposable income, creating divergent dynamics.
evidence_quotes: gold is priced out of the reach of many wage earners, especially in emerging markets. So there is a disparity between the demand by wealthy vs. poor people.
When the wealthy buy gold, they are putting the proceeds of the sale of other assets into it.
the poor have only US dollars to put into silver, if they have wages.

concepts.title: Gold-Silver Ratio and Silver's Upside Potential
concepts.summary: An elevated gold-silver ratio suggests silver has room to appreciate relative to gold, though past setups have been more favorable.
evidence_quotes: Silver certainly has the potential to rise in gold terms, especially with a gold-silver ratio over 80 as it is now.
There have been better setups for silver in the past than we see today.
the balance of risks suggests a better setup for silver is likely in the future.

concepts.title: Silver-Real Rates Correlation
concepts.summary: Silver prices are shown to be strongly negatively correlated with real interest rates across multiple time frames and frequencies.
evidence_quotes: Silver prices are strongly correlated to real rates.
silver (USD) is Negatively Correlated to Real Rates (US 10-year Treasury)
When real rates stopped falling in early August 2020, silver prices peaked shortly thereafter.

concepts.title: Silver as Monetary vs CPI Metal
concepts.summary: Silver is characterized as a monetary metal that tracks monetary inflation rather than consumer price inflation, explaining its stagnation despite high CPI.
evidence_quotes: Silver ignored the CPI inferno because it is not a CPI metal, it is a monetary metal and we were not witnessing monetary inflation.
it wasn’t monetary inflation, it was an increase in consumer prices

concepts.title: Reflation Expectations and Fiscal Stimulus
concepts.summary: Markets initially expected massive fiscal stimulus and political intervention to produce monetary reflation, boosting silver's outperformance versus gold.
evidence_quotes: markets expected monetary reflation and then economic recovery to be floated to victory on a wave of continuous wartime-like fiscal stimulus
Silver’s days of outperforming gold were numbered.

concepts.title: Fedwire Outage as Turning Point
concepts.summary: A mysterious multi-hour Fedwire system outage in February 2021 is identified as a pivotal event that shifted markets from reflation to retrenchment.
evidence_quotes: Fedwire went offline for several hours.
the root cause behind the disruption was identified quickly by staff and was not linked to a cybersecurity incident.
just two days after the Fedwire blackout, on February 26, the gold-silver ratio bottomed out.

concepts.title: Gold/Silver Ratio as Monetary Signal
concepts.summary: The gold-silver ratio is used as an indicator of monetary conditions, with rising ratios signaling deflationary scarcity and falling ratios signaling monetary expansion.
evidence_quotes: a rising ratio signals deflationary monetary circumstances
A falling ratio, i.e. silver gaining in relative value, signals the opposite, an expansion in monetary supply.

concepts.title: Post-Fedwire Market Reversals
concepts.summary: Multiple capital markets, currencies, and commodities reversed trend around the Fedwire disruption, indicating a broad shift away from reflationary expectations.
evidence_quotes: Below is a partial list of capital markets, currencies, commodities and balance sheet items that were affected
Reverse repurchase agreements: The Federal Reserve’s overnight Treasury security lending program experienced a sudden surge from nothing to USD 11bn

concepts.title: Quantitative Easing Ineffectiveness
concepts.summary: Decades of central bank base money expansion and quantitative easing failed to generate consumer price inflation until supply-chain shocks occurred.
evidence_quotes: quantitative easing, which has failed to revive moribund economies or stoke monetary creation everywhere it has been tried for the past 20 years
consumer prices effectively did the opposite of what authorities wanted: They remained muted and/or fell

concepts.title: Supply Chain Shock Inflation
concepts.summary: The recent surge in consumer prices is attributed to supply/demand imbalances and logistics disruptions rather than monetary expansion.
evidence_quotes: That increase was brought about by supply/demand imbalances and shocks, not by an expansion in money supply.
Not until supply chains were repeatedly electroshocked and economies randomly turned on and off like light switches did we witness consumer price rallies.

concepts.title: Shift Toward Inflationary Policy Regime
concepts.summary: The text argues crises are pushing politicians to abandon old economic institutions in favor of interventionist, inflation-fostering policies.
evidence_quotes: the old order – quantitative easing, globalization, WW2-era institutions – is to be abandoned and a new one
government-guaranteed bank loans, local supply, Universal Basic Income – to be fashioned
keep an eye on politicians’ announcements in favor of

concepts.title: Government Market Intervention
concepts.summary: Discusses specific government actions like price controls, tariffs, subsidies, and windfall taxes as signs of disabling free markets.
evidence_quotes: disabling markets, e.g. on March 17, 2022 Italy’s Ignazio Visco stated “Administered prices for a small period of time would not be a bad idea”
localizing industry, e.g. on March 16, 2022 the EU’s Valdis Dombrovskis announced tariffs against Indonesian and Indian steel
Italy’s Mario Draghi announced windfall taxes on Italian energy companies
France’s Jean Castex expanded and prolonged the state guarantees of bank loans

concepts.title: Silver Supply Stagnation
concepts.summary: Total silver supply has remained largely flat for over a decade despite modest annual growth forecasts.
evidence_quotes: total silver supply has remained effectively unchanged since 2010, averaging 1,037 Moz per year from 2010 through 2021
Overall supply, including both fundamental and speculative, grew 5.6% in 2021 to 1,025 million ounces (Moz)
This stagnation extends out through to 2025, which the industry consensus has penciled in for 1,100 Moz

concepts.title: Mine Supply Concentration (Mexico, Peru, China)
concepts.summary: Silver mine production is dominated by a few countries, with Mexico and Peru forecast to grow output significantly.
evidence_quotes: Mexico and Peru, the world’s top two producers, to account for just under one-third of global supply
increase production during 2021 by 10.6% and 7.5%, respectively
China is the only other country with a double-digit market share in global production

concepts.title: Silver Demand Categories and Forecasts
concepts.summary: Silver demand is split into industrial, ornamental, financial, and speculative categories, each with divergent and questionable growth forecasts.
evidence_quotes: Approximately 55% of demand is for industrial purposes in categories such as “electrical, electronics, batteries”
Ornamental demand is 24% of overall demand
Financial demand consists of government and private purchases of silver coins, medals and bars; it takes 18% of the overall demand pie
Speculative demand is the last category of silver demand

concepts.title: Silver Supply-Demand Deficit
concepts.summary: Analysts project silver demand will exceed supply annually through 2025, drawing down above-ground stockpiles.
evidence_quotes: analysts expect demand to outstrip supply in 2022 (and for every year thereafter, through to 2025)
resulting in a 135 Moz annual deficit in supply relative to demand
Those ounces will have to come from above-ground stock, which is estimated to be around 3,200 Moz

concepts.title: Financial Repression and Debt Burn-off
concepts.summary: The report predicts governments will use inflation and financial repression to erode high public and private debt levels over coming decades.
evidence_quotes: silver will take over and be pushed forward by the hot winds of inflation for a decade or two
governments burn off private and public debt levels via financial repression

concepts.title: Skepticism Toward Consensus Analyst Forecasts
concepts.summary: The authors repeatedly question overly optimistic consensus estimates for silver demand given negative macroeconomic conditions.
evidence_quotes: it is hard to understand why analysts are so optimistic when Europe is rationing energy, China is pursuing zero-Covid policies
These estimates are astonishing, because this category grows when consumers are experiencing rising levels of income
it is – again – hard to understand why mainstream economists are so negative on financial demand

concepts.title: Coppock Curve Momentum Indicator
concepts.summary: The Coppock curve is used as a long-term momentum indicator giving buy signals when it turns upward from below zero, currently on an upward trend since December 2021.
evidence_quotes: we once again refer to the Coppock curve, which has proved to be a reliable momentum indicator
Since the end of 2015, the indicator has been on “buy.”
since December 2021 it is now back on an upward trend

concepts.title: Cup-and-Handle Price Formation
concepts.summary: Gold's long-term chart shows a cup-handle formation projecting a price target of around USD 2,700 once resolved.
evidence_quotes: The long-term cup-handle formation, which could now soon be resolved, seems particularly interesting
The price target of the formation remains at around USD 2,700

concepts.title: Analyst Price Forecast Consensus
concepts.summary: Bloomberg analyst consensus forecasts for gold and silver show declining, sideways price targets through 2026, reflecting procyclical sentiment.
evidence_quotes: a median price of USD 1,900 is expected
De facto, the analysts therefore expect a sideways movement
a median price of USD 24 is expected, followed by a drop to USD 22.94 in 2023

concepts.title: Optix Sentiment Indicator
concepts.summary: The Optix Index from Sentimentrader measures market sentiment as a contrarian indicator, currently neutral for gold and near-bearish for silver.
evidence_quotes: One of our favorite sentiment indicators is the Optix Index from Sentimentrader
Currently, the Optix Index is at 49 and thus in neutral territory
The Optix Index for silver is currently trading at 39, close to bearish territory

concepts.title: Seasonal Price Patterns
concepts.summary: Gold and silver exhibit seasonal patterns in midterm election years, with headwinds in May-June and reversals in July.
evidence_quotes: seasonal headwinds set in from the end of May, but reverse again at the beginning of July
a strong seasonal uptrend can be seen from July. June marks the weakest month

concepts.title: Midas Touch Gold Model
concepts.summary: A quantitative multi-factor model synthesizing technical signals across markets that switched into bearish mode for gold on April 19.
evidence_quotes: The Midas Touch Gold Model™ switched into bearish mode on April 19
it succeeds in summarizing an extensive analysis compactly and clearly in a table and comes to a clear conclusion

concepts.title: Gold/Silver Ratio Signal
concepts.summary: The gold/silver ratio turned bearish due to silver's weakness, signaling that silver's outperformance phase remains distant.
evidence_quotes: The gold/silver ratio turned due to the weak development of the silver price that had already occurred on April 11
The sharp rise in the gold/silver ratio also makes it clear that we will have to be patient

concepts.title: Bitcoin/Gold Ratio
concepts.summary: Despite Bitcoin's outperformance versus gold in recent years, the current Bitcoin/gold ratio favors gold as a bullish signal.
evidence_quotes: Although Bitcoin has mercilessly outperformed gold in recent years, the Bitcoin/gold ratio currently favors gold
It currently takes just under 16 ounces of gold to equal one Bitcoin

concepts.title: US Dollar Index Strength
concepts.summary: The DXY's steep 12-month rally to a 21.5-year high is seen as overbought, with a potential decline below 103.40 turning bullish for gold.
evidence_quotes: The US Dollar Index rose by a good 17.3% in the last 12 months
the DXY is currently trading at its highest level in 21.5 years
Should the DXY fall below 103.40, this component within the Midas Touch Gold Model™ changes to bullish

concepts.title: Gold Price Technical Downtrend
concepts.summary: The daily chart shows gold falling sharply and breaking key support levels without much resistance.
evidence_quotes: the gold price fell from USD 1,998 to USD 1,799 without much resistance
the support zone around USD 1,850 was cracked within five trading days

concepts.title: 200-Day Moving Average
concepts.summary: The 200-day line is used as a key technical level that gold price recently broke through and may retest.
evidence_quotes: The 200-day line (currently USD 1,836) withstood the pressure of the bears for only two trading days.
lift the gold price at least back above the 200-day line
undergo a second test of its slightly rising 200-day line until midsummer

concepts.title: Stochastic Oscillator Oversold Signal
concepts.summary: The stochastic oscillator indicates an oversold market condition but has failed to signal a bottom.
evidence_quotes: The stochastic oscillator would actually be strongly oversold, but has nestled below 20 for 10 trading days

concepts.title: Market Crash Contagion Risk
concepts.summary: A broader liquidation wave from the bursting tech bubble could drag gold prices significantly lower, echoing 2008.
evidence_quotes: a merciless liquidation wave has been pulling the rug out from under all markets on a large scale for weeks
the gold price would certainly not be able to escape this crash scenario, similar to 2008's, and would probably reset to at least about USD 1,680

concepts.title: Seasonal Patterns in Gold
concepts.summary: Gold has historically performed poorly between March and July, with new upward trends more likely from August onward.
evidence_quotes: A bullish expectation has rarely paid off in the past between March and July
only from August onwards would the start of a new multi-month upward wave in the precious metals sector be conceivable

concepts.title: Coppock Indicator Buy Signal
concepts.summary: The long-term Coppock indicator generated a buy signal for gold at the end of 2015.
evidence_quotes: The Coppock indicator generated a longterm buy signal at the end of 2015.

concepts.title: Cup-and-Handle Formation
concepts.summary: A long-term cup-handle chart pattern in gold is resolving more slowly than anticipated.
evidence_quotes: The resolution of the long-term cup-handle formation is proving to be much tougher and more protracted than expected.

concepts.title: Sentiment and Speculative Shakeout
concepts.summary: Since gold's 2020 peak, a speculative shakeout has occurred, though an extreme bearish washout in sentiment has not yet materialized.
evidence_quotes: Since gold's all-time high in August 2020, a speculative shakeout has taken place, which should provide a healthy foundation for further price increases.
Although sentiment has clouded recently, an extreme bearish washout has not (yet) taken place.

concepts.title: Gold Relative Strength vs Silver and Miners
concepts.summary: Rising relative strength of gold compared to silver and mining stocks is seen as a cautionary technical signal.
evidence_quotes: The recent increase in the relative strength of gold versus silver and mining stocks also makes us cautious.

concepts.title: Monetary Policy Trilemma
concepts.summary: Central banks face a conflict between price stability, financial market stability, and economic support amid tightening.
evidence_quotes: the monetary policy trilemma – price stability vs. financial market stability vs. economic support – that we warned about is now a reality
the monetary policy showdown between price stability, economic activity, and financial market stability is now looming

concepts.title: Declining Central Bank Credibility
concepts.summary: Public confidence in the Federal Reserve has fallen sharply after mischaracterizing inflation as transitory.
evidence_quotes: Jerome Powell’s insistence that inflation was merely _transitory_ is now as legendary as Christine Lagarde’s belittling description of the inflation surge as a _hump_
Not surprisingly, confidence in central banking is in a steep decline.

concepts.title: Rapid Interest Rate Tightening
concepts.summary: The Fed raised rates faster and more aggressively than in prior cycles, causing financial system stress.
evidence_quotes: Jerome Powell raised interest rates twice as much in less than a third the time that Janet Yellen took in the last hiking cycle
The strongest and fastest interest rate hikes in the industrialized nations in over 40 years have already claimed their first victims.

concepts.title: Regional Bank Failures 2023
concepts.summary: A wave of US and European bank collapses, including SVB, Signature, First Republic, and Credit Suisse, signals financial fragility.
evidence_quotes: Silicon Valley Bank (SVB ) collapsed without warning, followed shortly by Signature Bank
Three of the four largest US bank failures in history took place in the past few weeks
with the venerable Credit Suisse, it is not just any bank that has been hit

concepts.title: Austrian Business Cycle Theory
concepts.summary: Excess liquidity creates artificial booms that are painfully unwound when stimulus is withdrawn.
evidence_quotes: Financial history is full of precedents where flooding the markets with liquidity triggers an artificial boom.
When the artificial stimuli are withdrawn, the misallocations are ruthlessly exposed and then cleaned up by painful price collapses, insolvencies, and recessions

concepts.title: Quantitative Tightening and Balance Sheet Reversal
concepts.summary: The Fed's balance sheet reduction program was interrupted by emergency liquidity injections during the banking crisis.
evidence_quotes: a key component of current policy is quantitative tightening, i.e. the reduction of the central bank’s balance sheet
the balance sheet total had to be inflated again by USD 400bn

concepts.title: Negative Money Supply Growth
concepts.summary: US M2 money supply is contracting for the first time since the Great Depression, historically linked to banking crises.
evidence_quotes: money supply growth in the US, calculated on a monthly basis, is negative for the first time since the 1950s, and on an annual basis for the first time since the Great Depression
whenever US M2 money supply has contracted on an annual basis, there’s been a banking crisis, a depression and/or deflation

concepts.title: Recession Warning Indicators
concepts.summary: Multiple indicators, including the inverted yield curve and weakening labor market, point to an imminent US recession.
evidence_quotes: the signs of an imminent recession in the USA are growing stronger
The strongly inverted yield curve, a slowly weakening labor market, the Conference Board Leading Economic Index (LEI) – all these leave little room for economic optimism

concepts.title: Future Inflationary Policy Response
concepts.summary: Future economic and market stress will likely prompt highly inflationary monetary and fiscal responses like QE and rate cuts.
evidence_quotes: the response will be highly inflationary: QE, YCC, and interest rate cuts

the longer and deeper the financial markets fall, the more stimulative, aggressive and desperate the monetary and fiscal policy responses will be, ultimately laying the foundation for another, higher wave of inflation

concepts.title: Bretton Woods III / New Monetary Order
concepts.summary: A proposed shift toward a commodity-backed monetary system in the East that weakens the Eurodollar system and drives Western inflation.
evidence_quotes: We are witnessing the birth of Bretton Woods III – a new world (monetary) order centered around commodity-based currencies in the East
From the Bretton Woods era backed by gold bullion, to Bretton Woods II backed by inside money
to Bretton Woods III backed by outside money (gold bullion and other commodities)

concepts.title: De-dollarization and Militarization of Money
concepts.summary: Countries, especially BRICS-aligned emerging markets, are reducing US dollar reserves and trade reliance due to sanctions and geopolitical risk.
evidence_quotes: these states that have been increasingly building up gold reserves and reducing US dollar reserves since 2008
The emerging-market countries have taken careful note of the _militarization of money_ and are now trying to reduce their dependence on the US dollar
efforts to reduce the role of the US dollar as a trading currency are increasing
these and other developments significantly undermine the _petrodollar system_

concepts.title: Central Bank Gold Accumulation
concepts.summary: Central banks, particularly in Asia and among energy exporters, have sharply increased gold purchases as a reserve diversification strategy.
evidence_quotes: Central banks have been net buyers of gold since 2009
In 2022, central banks increased their purchases by 152%, to over 1,136 tons
with Qatar, Iraq, and the United Arab Emirates, three major energy exporters are now among the top ten gold buyers
We expect that central bank demand will become a key driver of this gold bull market

concepts.title: BRICS Economic and Geopolitical Rise
concepts.summary: The growing economic weight and political assertiveness of BRICS nations relative to the G7 is reshaping global power dynamics.
evidence_quotes: The growing political self-confidence of the BRICS countries is a logical consequence of their increasing economic importance
these countries have had a higher aggregate GDP than the G7 countries since 2021
demographic situation also argues for significantly higher long-term growth potential in the BRICS countries than in the West

concepts.title: Thucydides Trap / US-China Rivalry
concepts.summary: The rise of China as a challenger power risks conflict with the established US hegemon, echoing historical great-power tensions.
evidence_quotes: it is fair to ask to what extent we are in the Thucydides Trap today
the rise of an emerging power leads to conflicts with the established world power
China’s growing strength and the resulting shift in the global power structure could lead to a warlike confrontation between the US and China

concepts.title: Resource Nationalism and Commodity Supercycle
concepts.summary: Rising resource nationalism and inelastic supply curves point to a structural commodity supercycle and stagflation risk.
evidence_quotes: Resource nationalism is gaining momentum
Chile... announced it would nationalize SQM and Albemarle
Global commodity supply curves may now be nearly vertical – a recipe for medium-term stagflation
The commodity supercycle... is clearly intact in our view

concepts.title: Fossilflation and Greenflation
concepts.summary: Energy supply constraints and green-transition demand are driving structurally higher fossil fuel and metal/mineral prices.
evidence_quotes: both _fossilflation_ , after the supplies of natural gas, oil, and coal decrease in succession, and _greenflation,_
meaning higher metal and mineral prices due to increased demand for green commodities

concepts.title: Gold Investment Demand and ETF Flows
concepts.summary: Investor demand for gold via ETFs remains subdued but could surge with FOMO once new all-time highs are reached.
evidence_quotes: investors will be looking to protect themselves from stubborn inflation, a possible recession, and increasing default risks
gold ETFs saw inflows again in March as a result of the banking crisis, this was after 10 straight months of outflows
Investment demand from gold ETFs could tip the gold price scales
at new all-time highs, _FOMO_ will kick in and new players will then enter the field

concepts.title: Federal Reserve Soft Landing Doubts
concepts.summary: Skepticism that the Federal Reserve can achieve a soft landing, with markets potentially exposing its restrictive policy as a bluff.
evidence_quotes: The soft landing much invoked by the Federal Reserve seems to become less likely by the day
whether it will be _called_ by the market and its strategy exposed as a bluff
The gold price already seems to anticipate that the restrictive US monetary policy will turn out to be a bluff

concepts.title: Gold Price All-Time Highs
concepts.summary: Gold reached new record highs in nearly all currencies except the US dollar, with the dollar-denominated price hitting its highest quarterly close ever.
evidence_quotes: the price of gold has marked new all-time highs in virtually every currency, with the notable exception of the US dollar
the gold price closed Q1/2023 at its highest quarterly level ever

concepts.title: Gold Bull Market Trend
concepts.summary: The long-term upward trend of gold is described as intact, with expectations of a new trend phase once dollar-denominated highs are reached.
evidence_quotes: The long-term upward trend of gold is clearly intact. The basis for further price increases seems excellent.
we assume that as soon as new all-time highs are reached in US dollar terms, the next trend phase of the gold bull market will be ushered in

concepts.title: US Dollar Strength Debate
concepts.summary: Analysts present competing views on whether the US dollar will weaken or strengthen going forward.
evidence_quotes: Michael Hartnett (BofA) and Brent Johnson make numerous arguments for a weaker and a firmer US dollar, respectively.

concepts.title: BIS Warning on Dollar Strength
concepts.summary: The Bank for International Settlements warned about risks stemming from an overly strong US dollar amid shifting dollar-commodity relationships.
evidence_quotes: The BIS recently warned of the risks of a (too) firm US dollar, especially against the background of a changing relationship between the US dollar and commodities.

concepts.title: Gold as Inflation Hedge
concepts.summary: Gold is portrayed as preserving purchasing power better than banknotes, immune to inflationary government policies.
evidence_quotes: No bet has been more certain to win in the centuries of monetary history than that a gold piece, inaccessible to the inflationary policies of governments, would preserve its purchasing power better than a banknote.

title: 05 Status Quo Of The Inflation Trend

concepts.title: Central Bank 'Transitory' Inflation Misjudgment
concepts.summary: Central bankers like Powell and Lagarde initially dismissed rising inflation as transitory or peaking, which proved inaccurate.
evidence_quotes: I think we now understand better how little we understand about inflation.
We see inflation as a hump and the hump eventually declines.
Transitory was the rise in inflation, no reason to worry.
the peak of the inflation wave had probably already been reached

concepts.title: Money Supply Expansion Driving Inflation
concepts.summary: Rapid M3 money supply growth during the pandemic laid the groundwork for the inflation surge, a warning that was ignored.
evidence_quotes: an expansion of the M3 money supply by more than 27% between January 2020 and April 2022 would provide the basis for high inflation were ignored
ignoring money supply expansion had been a mistake

concepts.title: Fed Average Inflation Targeting Shift
concepts.summary: The Fed's 2020 shift to an average 2% inflation target over an undefined period would now require sustained disinflation to achieve.
evidence_quotes: the Federal Reserve adjusted its inflation target to average 2% inflation over an undefined period
it would meanwhile take a strong and sustained disinflation, or better even a deflationary phase, for the Fed to hit its new inflation target again

concepts.title: US and Eurozone Inflation Persistence
concepts.summary: Both US and eurozone inflation remain well above 2% targets, with core inflation proving more persistent than headline figures.
evidence_quotes: the CPI (4.9%) and the PCE Index (4.6%) are still well above the inflation target of 2%
the inflation rate even reached double digits, at 10.6%
core inflation, is now higher than the headline inflation rate, and even shows a slight upward trend in the eurozone

concepts.title: Food and Fuel Prices Impact on Expectations
concepts.summary: Elevated food and gasoline prices disproportionately affect poorer households and strongly influence inflation expectations.
evidence_quotes: Currently, food has the highest inflation rate. This fact is worrisome for the formation of inflation expectations
gasoline prices are also still elevated, it is hardly surprising that poorer social strata in particular are affected by the inflation crisis

concepts.title: Bank of Japan Unconventional Monetary Policy
concepts.summary: Decades of ultra-loose BoJ policy (ZIRP, QE, YCC) have finally produced high inflation, seen as a blueprint for Western central banks.
evidence_quotes: For the first time since 1981, inflation exceeded 4% in January
1999: introduction of ZIRP
2013: QQE and the 2-2-2 plan – doubling the monetary base and achieving 2% inflation within 2 years
We believe that Western central banks are on the same path – only with a few years' delay

concepts.title: Temporary Disinflationary Factors in 2022
concepts.summary: Short-term factors like SPR releases, China's lockdown, and price caps artificially suppressed inflation readings in 2022.
evidence_quotes: the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) was reduced by 300 million barrels, or almost 50%
China's average oil consumption fell by 390,000 barrels per day compared to 2021, the first annual decline since 1990
euro area government measures lowered the inflation rate by a total of 0.6 percentage points

concepts.title: China Reopening Inflationary Potential
concepts.summary: China's post-lockdown reopening and accumulated savings could unleash pent-up demand, fueling medium-term inflationary pressures.
evidence_quotes: protests put an abrupt end to the zero-Covid policy, and China's economy is now open again
These have grown by over 50% in the past three pandemic years, and by USD 2.6trn in 2022 alone
continued expansionary monetary policy with falling borrowing costs will set inflationary dynamics in motion over the medium term

concepts.title: Second Inflation Wave Risk
concepts.summary: The report warns that a second, potentially more pronounced inflation wave is building after the current one subsides.
evidence_quotes: signs that indicate that a second, probably even more pronounced, wave of inflation is already building up, to hit after the current wave of inflation has subsided
The phenomena of this secondary wave may be quantitatively more important than those of the primary wave

concepts.title: Tequila Theory of Money (Lagged Effects)
concepts.summary: Monetary expansion and later tightening take time to filter into the real economy, causing delayed inflationary and disinflationary effects.
evidence_quotes: it takes quite some time for an expansion of the money supply to unfold in the real economy and drive up inflation rates
We also call this the _Tequila Theory of Money._
we have to warn about the lag effects, but this time in the opposite direction

concepts.title: Quantitative Tightening and Rate Hikes
concepts.summary: Central banks' shift to QT and rapid rate hikes is shrinking balance sheets and collapsing credit demand.
evidence_quotes: four consecutive 75 basis point rate hikes by the Federal Reserve were next to impossible
The effects of QT, the shrinking of the aggregate central bank balance sheet, and higher interest rates will now be felt more clearly
Credit demand is currently collapsing across the board before our eyes.

concepts.title: Everything Bubble Financial Fragility
concepts.summary: Structural changes—mobile banking, social media, options trading, and derivatives exposure—increase the risk and speed of financial market collapse.
evidence_quotes: the continued implosion of the so-called "Everything Bubble" is a realistic scenario

evidence_quotes: We present a modified version of the traditional 60/40 portfolio, which is derived from the new gold playbook
This consists of 60% equities and bonds and 40% alternative asset classes
These include physical gold, silver, mining stocks, commodities and Bitcoin

concepts.title: Long-Term Gold Price Forecast
concepts.summary: The report reaffirms a long-term gold price target of USD 4,800 by 2030, requiring a specific annualized return compared to past decades.
evidence_quotes: We are sticking to our gold price forecast of USD 4,800 by the end of 2030, which we presented in 2020
Achieving this price target requires an annualized return of just under 12%
the return in the 2000s was over 14% p.a., compared with around 27% p.a. in the 1970s

concepts.title: Debt Sustainability and Monetary Policy Tightening
concepts.summary: Rising interest rates amid high government debt levels, especially in Japan, raise concerns about debt sustainability and central bank policy limits.
evidence_quotes: The harsh end to the zero interest rate policy is reflected in sharply rising interest rates for overindebted Western countries
As the country with the highest level of debt, Japan has reached the limits of its debt sustainability
the price of gold in yen has more than doubled since 2020

title: 04 The Status Quo Of The Inflation Trend

concepts.title: Persistent Above-Target Inflation
concepts.summary: Inflation in the US and euro area has remained stubbornly above central bank targets for years, rarely dipping below 2%.
evidence_quotes: Stubbornly at a (slightly) higher level
The last time both inflation measures were below the 2% target was in February 2021, more than 4 years ago.
For the calendar year 2024, overall inflation of 2.9% (CPI) and 2.6% (PCE) in the US and 2.4% in the euro area was recorded.

concepts.title: Core Inflation Exceeding Headline
concepts.summary: Core inflation has consistently run higher than overall inflation, remaining above 2% for years in both the US and euro area.
evidence_quotes: As a result, the core inflation rate consistently exceeds the overall inflation rate.
In 2024, core inflation amounted to 3.2% (CPI), 2.8% (PCE), and 2.7% (HICP).
core PCE (the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure) has been above 2% since March 2021, that is, for over 4 years

concepts.title: Energy Price Effects on Inflation
concepts.summary: Falling and then volatile energy prices have significantly eased headline inflation figures since 2023.
evidence_quotes: the overall inflation rate on both sides of the Atlantic has been significantly eased by falling energy prices since the start of 2023
US natural gas futures had risen by 140% year-on-year to almost USD 5 per MMBtu
the significant decline in energy prices, particularly oil, in response to the global tariff conflict triggered by Donald Trump

concepts.title: Fed Average Inflation Targeting
concepts.summary: The Federal Reserve's average inflation targeting since 2020 is characterized as a covert increase in the inflation target.
evidence_quotes: the Federal Reserve has been aiming to achieve its inflation target on average since August 2020
this is nothing more than a covert increase in the US inflation target
US monetary policy would have to aim for an inflation rate of significantly below 2% for several years to achieve the inflation target of 2% on average

concepts.title: Service Sector Wage-Price Spiral
concepts.summary: Services are driving current inflation as delayed wage increases interact with reduced supply from business closures to sustain price pressures.
evidence_quotes: On both sides of the Atlantic, prices are being driven by services.
the (delayed) increase in wages in the services sector is leading to a pricewage spiral
insolvencies and business closures, which reduce supply and thus trigger additional price surges

concepts.title: Inflation's Political Fallout
concepts.summary: The 2024 'super-election year' saw governing parties lose votes broadly attributable to inflation's erosion of purchasing power perception.
evidence_quotes: 2024 was the year of elections. Almost half the world’s population was called to the polls
the governing parties lost votes significantly, while the opposition gained votes
the sharp rise in price levels compared to pre-inflationary times had a significant impact on the perception of lost purchasing power

concepts.title: Monetary vs Price Inflation Distinction
concepts.summary: The Austrian School distinguishes monetary inflation (money supply growth) from price inflation (its consequence), a distinction the report says is increasingly neglected.
evidence_quotes: Representatives of the Austrian School of Economics attach great importance to the distinction between monetary inflation and price inflation.
the monetary underfeed – money supply inflation – and the inevitable consequence of an excessive expansion of the money supply – price inflation
Inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon in the sense that it is and can be produced only by a more rapid increase in the quantity of money than in output.

concepts.title: Central Bank Quantitative Tightening
concepts.summary: Major central banks, especially the Fed and ECB, have been shrinking their balance sheets through QT, though the pace is now slowing.
evidence_quotes: The Federal Reserve has been engaged in QT since June 2022.
Since the all-time high in April 2022, the Federal Reserve has reduced its total assets by a quarter.
the pace of reduction for US Treasuries was significantly lowered from USD 25bn to USD 5bn per month
the ECB ceased all reinvestment of expiring bonds from the PEPP

concepts.title: BoJ Quantitative Tightening
concepts.summary: The Bank of Japan is reducing its balance sheet and JGB purchases while having ended yield curve control.
evidence_quotes: The BoJ announced its QT plan at the end of July 2024.
the BoJ relinquished yield curve control in October 2023
the BoJ had reduced its total balance sheet by just under 5%

concepts.title: Global M2 Money Supply Growth
concepts.summary: Broad money supply growth is reaccelerating across major economies after 2023 contractions, with varying regional rates.
evidence_quotes: M2 is now expanding again at over 3% year-on-year
In China, growth is significantly higher at around 7%
Global liquidity growth in US dollars is currently over 3% year-onyear

concepts.title: Administrative/Carbon Tax Inflation
concepts.summary: CO2-related taxes and carbon border measures like ETS-II and CBAM are identified as bureaucratic drivers of inflation.
evidence_quotes: taxes designed to reduce CO2 emissions
the _Emission Trading System II_ (ETS-II) will come into effect from 2027
the climate tariff, the _European Carbon Border Adjustment_ (CBAM)... will have direct and indirect inflationary effects

concepts.title: US Tariffs and Inflation Debate
concepts.summary: There is disagreement over whether Trump's tariffs will cause lasting inflation or only a transitory price adjustment.
evidence_quotes: some believe that tariffs will always be borne exclusively by consumers
Nothing is more transitory than tariffs if it’s a one-time price adjustment
in the short term, Donald Trump’s tariff policy is likely to have an inflationary effect in the US

concepts.title: Rearmament-Driven Inflation
concepts.summary: Large-scale, debt-financed military buildups are seen as inflationary due to competing resource demand and labor supply effects.
evidence_quotes: Inflationary effects are almost unavoidable in the case of large-scale armament build-ups
EUR 150bn is to be raised by the EU Commission as part of the _ReArm Europe/Readiness 2030_ program
demographic change will significantly reduce labor supply in the coming years and thus increase inflationary pressure

concepts.title: Fiscal Theory of the Price Level
concepts.summary: The FTPL explains inflation as arising from lack of confidence in government's ability to meet future fiscal obligations, not just money supply growth.
evidence_quotes: the so-called _Fiscal Theory of the Price Level_ (FTPL)
inflation occurs when the present value of future government expenditure exceeds the present value of future government revenue
the money supply – issued by the central banks – should be viewed as a perpetual, non-interest-bearing bond

concepts.title: PMI as Economic Growth Indicator
concepts.summary: Purchasing Managers' Index trends signal slowing US growth and stagnant euro area activity near the expansion/contraction threshold.
evidence_quotes: The Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) is pointing clearly downward
the PMI has been hovering around the 50-point mark for over a year
which is the dividing line between expansion (above 50) and contraction (below 50)

concepts.title: Wage Growth and Inflation
concepts.summary: Elevated nominal wage growth in the US and euro area, driven by labor shortages and demographics, continues to support inflation.
evidence_quotes: Nominal wage growth in the US and the euro area remains significantly higher than before the wave of inflation
wage pressure in the lower-income segment is likely to increase due to tighter immigration policies
demographic change will strengthen the bargaining power of employees

concepts.title: AI's Deflationary/Inflationary Effects
concepts.summary: AI may boost productivity and reduce inflation long-term, but its high energy demands could cause short-term inflationary pressure.
evidence_quotes: AI could be deflationary. This is one of the impacts of this technology that is most underappreciated
AI certainly has the potential to gradually increase productivity in many work processes
the high energy requirements of AI systems... could also trigger inflationary effects

concepts.title: Market-Based Inflation Expectations
concepts.summary: Long-term market inflation expectations, such as the 5-year, 5-year forward rate, have declined and shown volatility around policy events.
evidence_quotes: 5-year, 5-year inflation expectations
Very long-term inflation expectations have been on a downward trend since the fall of 2023
these inflation expectations plummeted by 16 basis points before shooting up sharply by 23 basis points

concepts.title: Break-even Inflation Rate
concepts.summary: Explains the break-even rate as the inflation level equalizing real returns between inflation-linked and conventional bonds, noting its weak predictive power.
evidence_quotes: The break-even inflation rate indicates the inflation rate required to ensure that the purchase of an inflation-linked bond yields at least the same real interest rate
the predictive power of breakeven rates is not particularly high, as evidenced by a comparison with actual inflation

concepts.title: Oil Price and Breakeven Divergence
concepts.summary: Discusses the recent divergence between the 2-year breakeven inflation rate and the WTI oil price, which are normally closely correlated.
evidence_quotes: there has been a clear divergence between the otherwise closely positively correlated oil price and the 2-year break-even rate
the WTI price should be around USD 80; if the oil price is used as a benchmark, the 2-year break-even rate should be more than 50 basis points lower

concepts.title: Survey-Based Inflation Expectations (Michigan)
concepts.summary: Describes the sharp rise in University of Michigan short- and long-term inflation expectations following the 2024 US elections.
evidence_quotes: Short-term inflation expectations have risen sharply since the US elections in November 2024 and already stand at 6.5% as of April
Long-term inflation expectations have also risen sharply year-on-year, by 1.4 percentage points or 50% to 4.4%

concepts.title: Political Bias in Fed Trust and Expectations
concepts.summary: Explains how party affiliation and perceived in-group/out-group status of the Federal Reserve shape trust and inflation expectations.
evidence_quotes: confirms the strong influence of party preferences on trust in the Federal Reserve and thus on inflation expectations
Trust is higher when the Federal Reserve is perceived as part of one’s own group. And higher trust correlates with lower inflation expectations
This has a direct impact on inflation expectations and seriously calls into question their predictive value

concepts.title: Euro Area Inflation Expectations vs ECB Target
concepts.summary: Compares consumer inflation expectations, which remain above the ECB's 2% target, with the more optimistic ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters.
evidence_quotes: inflation expectations in the euro area remain well above the ECB’s inflation target at 2.9% over the next 12 months and 2.5% over the next three years
The ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters is much more optimistic with regard to inflation trends
An inflation rate of around or even exactly 2.0% is expected for 2025, 2026, 2027, and long-term

concepts.title: Unreliability of Inflation Forecasts
concepts.summary: Argues that both market-based and survey-based inflation forecasts, as well as central bank forecasts, are frequently inaccurate.
evidence_quotes: both market-based and survey-based inflation expectations are very often wrong
Central banks are just as wrong with their inflation forecasts as the markets (or survey-based inflation expectations)
the current monetary policy is seen as appropriate, indeed must be seen as appropriate

concepts.title: China Exporting Deflation
concepts.summary: Describes how falling Chinese producer and export prices, driven by structural imbalances and tariffs, are exporting deflationary pressure globally.
evidence_quotes: producer prices have been in deflationary territory again since mid-2024. China is therefore exporting deflation
China’s price dynamics, driven by persistent structural imbalances and a weak renminbi, are likely to exert disinflationary, if not deflationary, pressure on global markets

concepts.title: Persistent Japanese Inflation and Negative Real Yields
concepts.summary: Notes Japan's unusually persistent above-target inflation and continued negative real yields despite the BoJ ending yield curve control.
evidence_quotes: Not since the early 1990s has inflation in Japan remained so stubbornly above the 2% mark
Although the BoJ officially ended yield curve control in March 2024, real yields are still in clearly negative territory

concepts.title: Gold as Hedge in Yen
concepts.summary: Highlights gold's strong multi-year performance in Japanese yen as an attractive alternative to unappealing bonds.
evidence_quotes: bonds are not very attractive to Japanese investors. Gold is all the more attractive
Since August 2018, gold has gained 230% in Japanese yen terms
Gold in yen has recorded consistent gains for 7 years

concepts.title: Budgetary Nonchalance and Fiscal-Monetary Merger
concepts.summary: Describes the erosion of fiscal discipline and the blurring of monetary and fiscal policy, exemplified by Germany's large spending funds and ECB-EU cooperation.
evidence_quotes: the first and most important sign of monetary climate change was the arrival of budgetary nonchalance
Germany has shed its previous fiscal virtue and moved into the camp of budgetary nonchalance
The second sign, the merging of monetary and fiscal policy, is also becoming increasingly obvious, especially in the euro area

concepts.title: Central Bank Political Independence Erosion
concepts.summary: Argues that central banks like the ECB and Fed are increasingly intertwined with politics, undermining claims of independence.
evidence_quotes: The ECB no longer even has the appearance of independence
The close links between politics and central banks can also be seen in personnel decisions
the central bank is a codependent part of the government, the interest rate-manipulating and bond-buying branch of the Treasury

concepts.title: Elevated Inflation Volatility
concepts.summary: Notes that the early 2020s saw historically high inflation volatility across major economies, linked partly to central bank misjudgments.
evidence_quotes: The first four years of the 2020s were characterized by historically unprecedented inflation volatility in the euro area
The blatant miscalculations by leading central bankers when the wave of inflation took off in the course of 2021 also contributed to the substantial inflation volatility

concepts.title: Federal Reserve Political Independence Myth
concepts.summary: The text argues the Fed's independence is illusory, as it has been used to finance government deficits and remains politically aligned.
evidence_quotes: the independence of the Federal Reserve is a myth
the Federal Reserve was actively involved in financing Washington’s budget deficits through the printing press
an agency that is unable to withstand political pressure must ultimately be considered part of the government

concepts.title: Political Pressure Driving Inflation
concepts.summary: Empirical research shows that political pressure on central banks raises inflation and inflation expectations.
evidence_quotes: the exertion of political pressure on the central bank does indeed promote inflation
A shock in the form of higher political pressure on the Federal Reserve not only increased inflation significantly but also led to higher inflation expectations
A truly independent central bank...would therefore be a genuine institutional inflation hedge

concepts.title: Central Bank Leadership Succession
concepts.summary: Upcoming political appointments of Fed and ECB leaders will reflect prevailing monetary policy agendas.
evidence_quotes: The political wrangling over the appointment of a new Federal Reserve Chairman in May 2026 and ECB President in November 2027
the responsible political bodies will make the appointments in line with their own economic and monetary policy ideas

concepts.title: Incrementum Inflation Signal
concepts.summary: A proprietary signal tracking shifts between inflationary, neutral, and deflationary regimes has shown increased volatility recently.
evidence_quotes: the Incrementum Inflation Signal has shown a significantly increased frequency of signal changes
the signal predominantly indicated a positive inflationary environment
we expect the signal – much like in 2020 – to once again be able to anticipate an upcoming wave of inflation

concepts.title: Commodity Market Divergence
concepts.summary: Gold and energy commodities have moved in opposite directions, leaving broad commodity indices flat.
evidence_quotes: pronounced divergence within commodity markets over the past twelve months
While gold experienced a significant upward trend, energy commodities came under continued downward pressure
reflected in the overall stable, yet sluggish development of the Bloomberg Commodity Index

concepts.title: Categorized Inflation Drivers
concepts.summary: The text organizes current inflation forces into short-, medium-, and long-term inflationary and disinflationary dynamics.
evidence_quotes: Short-term disinflationary dynamics
Medium-term inflationary dynamics
Long term structural inflationary dynamics
Structural government debt

concepts.title: Historical Inflation Cycle Analogy
concepts.summary: A comparison between the 1966-1983 and post-2013 inflation cycles suggests a coming second, larger inflation wave.
evidence_quotes: The parallelism of the inflation trend in 1966–1983 and since 2013 is still striking
inflation in the US should move sideways until the end of the year and rise sharply in 2026 to around 11% in late summer 2028
we would now be in the calm before the second, stronger inflationary storm

concepts.title: Implicit Inflation Target Erosion
concepts.summary: Central banks' tolerance of persistently high inflation effectively raises their inflation target without formal acknowledgment.
evidence_quotes: The widespread nonchalance of leading central bankers towards the persistently high level of inflation is having the effect of a tacit increase in the inflation target
Implicit easing of the inflation target of 2%
The basic stance of those responsible for (monetary) policy is and remains inflationary

concepts.title: Record Gold Demand and Central Bank Buying
concepts.summary: Gold demand hit a record in 2024, driven by strong investor and central bank purchases, especially from emerging markets.
evidence_quotes: Gold demand reached a record high of 4,974 t in 2024
Central bank demand for gold not only exceeded 1,000 t for the third year in a row, but also reached a new all-time high of 1,086 t
Poland (90 t), India (73 t), and China (44 t) topped the list of central banks buying gold

concepts.title: Gold Supply and Recycling Trends
concepts.summary: Gold supply rose slightly in 2024, with recycling contributing an increasing share.
evidence_quotes: The gold supply of 4,974 t was slightly higher than in the previous year
gold recycling gaining in importance, with an increase of 11%

title: 11 Bringing It Home Central Bank Gold Repatriation

concepts.title: Central Bank Gold Repatriation Trend
concepts.summary: Since 2011, central banks have increasingly moved physical gold reserves from foreign vaults back to domestic storage, creating a self-reinforcing trend.
evidence_quotes: Gold repatriation refers to the process by which central banks move their physical gold reserves from the vaults of foreign gold custodians and back to vault storage within their own countries.
gold repatriation gained significant momentum starting in 2011 and has continued to the present day
the gold repatriation trend can be seen as an interconnected phenomenon that has created a noticeable domino effect

concepts.title: Sanctions Risk and Reserve Weaponisation
concepts.summary: Fear that reserves could be frozen or sanctioned by the US, EU, and G7 drives central banks to repatriate gold and diversify away from foreign custodians.
evidence_quotes: With the US, the EU, and the G7 active in imposing sanctions and freezing and confiscating foreign reserves, central banks repatriate gold and keep it under sovereign control
concerns about the weaponisation of reserves and rising US debt
the weaponisation of central bank reserves makes gold more attractive

concepts.title: Counterparty Risk of Foreign-Held Gold
concepts.summary: Gold stored abroad carries counterparty and confiscation risk, which the 2007/2008 financial crisis highlighted, reinforcing the value of domestic storage.
evidence_quotes: Physical gold has no counterparty risk, but this is only fully true when the gold is stored domestically rather than deposited abroad.
The 2007/2008 global financial crisis triggered central banks to reappraise counterparty risk and reinforced the importance of unencumbered gold stored in domestic vaults.

concepts.title: Motivations for Third-Party Gold Storage
concepts.summary: Despite repatriation trends, central banks still store gold abroad for security, liquidity/market access, and diversification of storage risk.
evidence_quotes: Security and physical safety: These institutions are known for their highly secure vaults with advanced physical and surveillance security
Liquidity and market access: The Bank of England in London offers central banks the ability to buy, store, and sell gold all in the same location
Diversification of storage risk: Storing a percentage of gold reserves in a stable foreign jurisdiction allows central banks to diversify storage risk

concepts.title: Survey Evidence of Repatriation Growth
concepts.summary: Multiple institutional surveys (Invesco, WGC, OMFIF) document rising shares of central banks holding gold domestically and citing geopolitical hedging motives.
evidence_quotes: 68% said they held physical gold in their own country, compared with 50% in 2020
74% of respondents said they would hold physical gold in their own country by 2028
geopolitical instability is among the top three reasons why central banks invest in gold, with 76% of emerging-market central banks indicating so
the two primary motivations of central banks are (a) holding gold in reserve portfolios are diversification (68% of respondents) and (b) as a hedge against geopolitical risk (40% of respondents)

concepts.title: Freezing of Central Bank Assets
concepts.summary: Historical instances of frozen central bank assets, especially Russia's 2022 reserves, illustrate the political risk of holding gold or reserves with foreign custodians.
evidence_quotes: these events have led to the freezing of central bank assets, e.g. assets of the central bank of Iran (USD 1.9bn frozen in 2010)
the largest of them all, the Russian central bank, which saw an estimated USD 258bn was frozen in 2022
Political risks must be considered because gold accounts can be frozen

concepts.title: Decline of Fed/BoE Vault Share
concepts.summary: The proportion of global official gold reserves stored outside the Federal Reserve and Bank of England has risen sharply, signaling shifting financial power.
evidence_quotes: The share of global official gold reserves not stored at the Federal Reserve and Bank of England has reached 78% in 2024, from 51% in 1972.
This shift can be seen as a proxy for the West's decline in financial dominance.

concepts.title: Link Between Gold Buying and Repatriation
concepts.summary: Central bank gold purchases and repatriation are driven by the same underlying geopolitical and trust concerns, making the two trends intertwined.
evidence_quotes: Central bank gold buying and repatriation trends are now inextricably linked and intertwined.
Central banks are buying gold because of rising geopolitical risk and the weaponisation of reserves via sanctions. But they are also repatriating gold for these very same reasons.

concepts.title: Venezuela Gold Repatriation
concepts.summary: Venezuela repatriated 160 tonnes of gold from Europe in 2011-2012 to assert sovereignty amid US sanction threats.
evidence_quotes: the central bank completed the repatriation of monetary gold , which began in late 2011
160 t of Venezuela’s gold was flown back from Europe to Caracas on 23 cargo flights
Catalysed by the threat of US sanctions and a desire to reduce dependence on Western financial institutions

concepts.title: Reserve Diversification Away From West
concepts.summary: Venezuela shifted FX reserves and gold away from Western institutions toward BRICS countries as a strategic hedge.
evidence_quotes: moving international FX reserves away from Western financial institutions and investing them with banks in the BRICS countries of China, Russia, and Brazil

concepts.title: Foreign Gold Confiscation Risk
concepts.summary: Gold left in foreign custody, like Venezuela's Bank of England holdings, can be frozen for political reasons.
evidence_quotes: 50.87 t left in the Bank of England in London to be used in “international financial operations”
this was the Venezuelan gold that the Bank of England then froze in 2018/2019 on instructions from the British Foreign Office, the US Treasury, and US State Department

concepts.title: Germany's Gold Repatriation Movement
concepts.summary: Public and political pressure forced the Bundesbank to repatriate 674 tonnes of gold from New York and Paris over 2013-2017.
evidence_quotes: Venezuela’s gold repatriation in 2011/2012 helped spark Germany’s gold repatriation movement
The campaign argued that 100% of the German gold should return to backstop the Bundesbank’s balance sheet and ensure future currency cover
completing the repatriation process a full 56 months after the 2013 plan was announced

concepts.title: Lack of Central Bank Gold Audits
concepts.summary: Bundesbank rarely physically audited gold held abroad, relying instead on written confirmations from custodians.
evidence_quotes: the Bundesbank rarely checked Germany’s New York gold reserves, visiting the Manhattan vaults only twice (in 2007 and 2011)
No physical audits had ever been conducted in New York, London, or Paris, with the Bundesbank relying on written confirmations
auditors were shown gold in one compartment, with only a few bars pulled out and weighed

concepts.title: Gold Swaps and Low-Purity Resmelting
concepts.summary: Repatriated gold showed signs of prior gold swap arrangements, with low-purity bars resmelted to hide origins.
evidence_quotes: strengthened suspicions that the German gold stored abroad had either disappeared or was involved in international gold swap arrangements with foreign central banks
a mere 5 t of low-purity gold from New York, which was resmelted to obscure its origins
85 t from New York, with 50 t of low-purity gold resmelted for the same reason

concepts.title: Netherlands Gold Storage Transparency
concepts.summary: Dutch officials faced political pressure to disclose and repatriate gold reserves held mostly abroad.
evidence_quotes: it is not practicable to have 90 percent of Dutch gold reserves abroad
only 67 t of the Dutch gold, i.e. less than 11%, was stored in Amsterdam, with the rest held “abroad”
in November 2014, the DNB than made a surprise announcement, saying that it had repatriated 122.5 t of gold from the New York Federal Reserve to Amsterdam

concepts.title: Gold as Anchor of Trust
concepts.summary: Central banks and commentators describe gold as a foundational trust asset during financial system stress.
evidence_quotes: Gold is the ultimate anchor of trust, especially during times of financial unrest and panic
it’s the anchor of trust for the financial system. If the system collapses, the gold stock can serve as a basis to build it up again

concepts.title: US-EU Tensions Reviving Repatriation Debate
concepts.summary: Renewed geopolitical friction between the US and EU has reignited calls to repatriate gold stored in New York.
evidence_quotes: The growing tensions between the US and the EU has reignited the discussion about repatriating the gold reserves stored in New York
called for the immediate repatriation of 1,236 t of German gold, or almost 37% of the total German gold reserves, from New York

concepts.title: Gold Storage Concentration Risk
concepts.summary: Audits and central banks flagged the risk of storing a disproportionate share of gold reserves in a single foreign vault like the Bank of England.
evidence_quotes: a high concentration risk
The gold depository contract with the Bank of England contained deficiencies.
There was no concept for carrying out the audit for gold holdings stored abroad.

concepts.title: Federal Reserve Gold Data Discrepancy
concepts.summary: Comparing New York Fed earmarked gold outflow data against Bundesbank and DNB reported withdrawals revealed unexplained tonnage gaps.
evidence_quotes: Federal Reserve data shows only 176.8 t were removed, leaving a 30.7-tonne discrepancy.
Bundesbank reported withdrawing 99 t, while Federal Reserve data recorded 129 t, an excess of 30 t
Numbers don’t lie.

concepts.title: Geopolitical and Sanctions Risk Motivations
concepts.summary: Central banks cited geopolitical tensions, sanctions exposure, and reduced reliance on the US dollar as key drivers for repatriating gold.
evidence_quotes: driven by distrust of foreign custodians, increasing geopolitical tensions, a Turkish lira crisis, and a desire to reduce reliance on the US dollar
in order to reduce geopolitical risk
suggest that the RBI gold movements were in response to heightened sanctions risks

concepts.title: Gold as Trusted Reserve Asset
concepts.summary: Gold is portrayed as the ultimate reserve asset that diversifies geopolitical risk and anchors trust during crises.
evidence_quotes: Gold is the “most reserve” of reserve assets: it diversifies geopolitical risk and is a kind of anchor of trust, especially in times of tension and crisis.

concepts.title: Failed Gold Repatriation Attempts
concepts.summary: Political opposition and central bank resistance blocked repatriation efforts in Switzerland, Romania, and Slovakia.
evidence_quotes: there have been failures due mainly to political and central bank resistance
the referendum clearly failed
This led to the bill’s effective shelving, and the Romanian gold remained in London.

concepts.title: Gold Lending Arrangements
concepts.summary: France's gold repatriation was linked to a shift in its gold lending strategy that removed the need for London storage.
evidence_quotes: likely driven by France’s decision to offer gold lending in collaboration with J.P. Morgan, eliminating the need for London storage

concepts.title: Gold Bar Purity and Resmelting
concepts.summary: Data discrepancies suggest the Bundesbank received low-purity gold bars from the Fed that had to be resmelted to hide their origin.
evidence_quotes: 50 t of which it was forced to resmelt to disguise the bars’ origins
suggests that the bars received were low-purity gold from the US Treasury’s gold holdings at the New York Federal Reserve

concepts.title: China's Covert Gold Accumulation
concepts.summary: The PBoC secretly buys gold in London and moves it to Beijing, effectively repatriating and shielding it from sanctions risk.
evidence_quotes: The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) regularly buys gold internationally, mainly in London, and promptly moves it back to Beijing.
Jan Nieuwenhuijs estimates that the PBoC has accumulated 1,000 t of gold since the West froze Russia’s FX reserves in early 2022.

concepts.title: Russia's Sanctions-Driven Gold Reserves
concepts.summary: Russia has steadily built domestic gold reserves stored only within the country to protect against Western sanctions and financial weaponization.
evidence_quotes: Russia is increasing its gold holdings because gold is a reserve asset that is free from legal and political risks.
Russia’s central bank has also been highly perceptive in recognizing sanctions risks and has steadily built its gold reserves from 400 t in 2007 to over 2,300 t today.
Russia has strategically prepared for geopolitical threats and ensured that its gold holdings are also protected from Western sanctions

concepts.title: Bank of England Vault Flows as Indicator
concepts.summary: Monthly Bank of England gold vault data reveals net outflows correlating with major central bank repatriation events and geopolitical shocks.
evidence_quotes: the Bank of England publishes end of month data on total gold held in its London vaults
a sizeable 434 t of gold flowed out of the Bank of England vaults, suggesting that Venezuela’s actions likely prompted other central banks to follow suit
Triggered by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the Bank of England’s vaults also saw consistent monthly gold outflows from January 2022 to March 2023, with a net loss of 574 t.

concepts.title: Sanctions Weaponization Eroding Trust
concepts.summary: The freezing of Russian FX reserves shocked central banks into reassessing gold and revealed distrust in Western financial institutions.
evidence_quotes: The West’s freezing of Russian FX reserves appears to have been a defining moment that shocked many of the world’s central banks into reassessing the importance of gold as a reserve asset.
The CBRT reduced its gold reserves abroad due to sanctions and tensions in relations with the US.
revealing the erosion of trust in the traditional financial institutions in the City of London and Manhattan

concepts.title: Gold and Silver Recycling Supply
concepts.summary: Recycling, mainly from jewelry, supplies about 25% of global gold and 18% of silver, with volumes rising alongside gold prices.
evidence_quotes: Around 25% of the global gold supply and approximately 18% of the silver supply come from recycling.
In 2023, recycled gold increased by 8.6%, followed by a 10.9% increase in 2024.
The most significant source of gold recycling is jewelry, accounting for 90%, while for silver it is the industrial sector.

concepts.title: Price Sensitivity of Recycling Supply
concepts.summary: Gold recycling supply responds strongly to price rises, whereas silver recycling is less price-sensitive and driven by industrial demand.
evidence_quotes: Price is the key factor influencing the recycling supply, with jewelry being particularly sensitive.
Silver recycling is less price-sensitive and mostly driven by industrial demand.
Before 2015, scrap gold peaked at 42% of supply (2009).

concepts.title: Urban Mining Concept
concepts.summary: Urban mining reclaims gold and silver from e-waste and jewelry, offering a sustainable, lower-emission alternative to traditional mining.
evidence_quotes: Urban mining refers to reclaiming valuable materials, such as gold and silver, from urban waste streams, including electronic waste (e-waste), old jewelry
Gold recycling is more flexible, faster, and more sustainable than mining, with savings of up to 90% in CO2 emissions.
There’s more gold in a ton of discarded electronics than in a ton of gold ore.

concepts.title: Peak Gold Theory

The Simon-Ehrlich wager best illustrates this philosophical divide.

concepts.title: Peak Gold Supply Debate
concepts.summary: Discusses forecasts that global gold mine supply will peak due to declining new discoveries, contrasted with historical evidence against a definitive peak.
evidence_quotes: peak gold proponents argue that global gold supply is finite
global annual gold supply will peak in 2026 at 110 Moz or 3,420 t
As for peak gold, it’s already here
a definitive peak in gold mining has not materialized

concepts.title: Gold Recycling as Supply Buffer

evidence_quotes: the gold recycling market would likely serve as a buffer against supply deficits

recycled gold reached 1,237 t in 2023, thus representing 25.3% of the total global gold supply

concepts.title: Jewelry Recycling Dominance
concepts.summary: Jewelry recycling is the largest and most traditional source of recycled gold, varying by regional cultural traditions.

higher rates in countries with a strong gold jewelry tradition like India

concepts.title: E-Waste as Gold Source

up to 15% of the world’s gold supply could be derived from e- waste by 2030

concepts.title: Above-Ground Gold Stock Composition

only approximately 0.5% of the total above-ground stock of gold is being recycled annually

concepts.title: Price Elasticity of Gold Recycling
concepts.summary: Gold recycling supply responds to price changes, acting as a price taker globally but sometimes a local price driver.

elasticity of recycling gold at a value of 3, implying that a 1% increase in the gold price results in a 3% increase in recycled gold supply

concepts.title: Currency Crises Driving Recycling
concepts.summary: Economic distress and currency crises significantly increase gold recycling as people liquidate holdings for cash.
evidence_quotes: Currency crises and economic recessions are additional powerful catalysts for gold recycling
Egyptian scrap supply exploded from 6t in Q4/2015 to 27t in Q2/2016

concepts.title: Gold Stock-to-Flow Ratio
concepts.summary: The stock-to-flow ratio measures gold's scarcity by comparing existing stock to annual production, signaling low inflationary pressure.
evidence_quotes: the total stock-to-flow ratio (SFR) for gold

A high ratio, typical for gold or Bitcoin, indicates scarcity and signals lower inflationary pressure

concepts.title: Gold Stock-to-Flow and Peak Gold
concepts.summary: Stable gold per-capita stock despite population growth undermines the peak gold theory, showing supply keeps pace with demand.

concepts.title: Price as Market Signal for Gold Supply
concepts.summary: Free price determination allows gold prices to signal scarcity and coordinate recycling supply and demand.
evidence_quotes: As long as there is a free price determination mechanism, absent price controls or similar interventions, the gold price can function as a signal to all market participants

concepts.title: Silver's Industrial Consumption vs Gold

a portion of all silver ever mined disappears irrecoverably, for example due to abrasion (coins) or as silver-containing solid waste and solutions

concepts.title: Silver Recycling Supply Dynamics

significant decreases in available silver scrap supply tend to support price levels, whereas considerable increases tend to limit price appreciation

concepts.title: Silver Price-Stock Disconnection

fabricated products demonstrate far less price sensitivity than silver bullion, again, due to the “immobility” of the silver

concepts.title: Recycling and Carbon Footprint Reduction

evidence_quotes: the production of one ounce of gold through traditional mining emits, on average about 1 t of CO2

concepts.title: Geopolitical and Strategic Value of Recycling

concepts.title: Geographic Structure of Gold Recycling Market

high-grade scrap is typically refined in its country of origin

concepts.title: Iran Attack Energy Price Shock

the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz – initially by Iran and, since midApril, also by the US – has nearly completely shut down this lifeline

concepts.title: Persistent US Inflation Above Target

the HICP fell below the ECB's inflation target of 2.0% in January and February

concepts.title: Declining Oil Intensity of Economies
